title: SGLang-Diffusion launched
description: LMSYS Org launched SGLang-Diffusion, extending the SGLang serving runtime to image and video diffusion models. The first wave shipped with FLUX, Stable Diffusion 3, and Qwen Image support, and reused SGLang's scheduler and KV-style caches for end-to-end diffusion serving.

title: Miles RL framework introduced
description: LMSYS Org introduced Miles, an enterprise-facing reinforcement learning framework for LLM and VLM post-training, as a joint effort with InfiXAI, Ant Group, and the SGLang RL team. Miles co-evolves with the slime project and targets large-scale MoE post-training.

title: Unified FP8 for stable MoE RL training
description: LMSYS Org published Unified FP8, a recipe to move beyond mixed-precision and run MoE reinforcement learning end-to-end in FP8 with stable convergence. The blog accompanied Miles updates and showed accelerated MoE RL training without quality regressions on representative MoE checkpoints.

title: Native NVIDIA Model Optimizer integration
description: LMSYS published a deep dive on SGLang's native NVIDIA Model Optimizer integration for seamless quantization and deployment, with reported up to 2x per-GPU throughput on Blackwell hardware spanning DGX Spark to GB300 NVL72.

title: SGLang v0.5.6 released
description: SGLang v0.5.6 added DeepSeek V3.2 / V3.2 Speciale support, blockwise diffusion language models, day-0 support for new diffusion models (Flux2, Z-image), introduced JIT Kernels, upgraded to PyTorch 2.9, and shipped Kimi-K2-Thinking model enhancements plus DeepSeek-v3-fp4 / GLM-4.6 / Kimi-K2 performance work.

title: SGLang v0.5.7 released
description: SGLang v0.5.7 shipped day-0 support for Mimo-V2-Flash, Nemotron-Nano-v3, and LLaDA 2.0; SGLang-Diffusion gained Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-Edit support, EAGLE 3 speculative-decoding draft models, plus Model Gateway v0.3.0 with scalable pipeline parallelism, dynamic chunking for ultra-long contexts, and encoder disaggregation for multimodal models.

title: EPD: elastic encoder scaling for VLMs
description: LMSYS published EPD Disaggregation in SGLang — an elastic-encoder-scaling architecture for vision-language models that lets the multimodal encoder scale independently from prefill and decode workers, improving GPU utilization and latency for production VLM serving.

title: Pipeline parallelism scales SGLang to million-token contexts
description: LMSYS detailed SGLang's chunked pipeline parallelism design that scales context windows past one million tokens. The post covered scheduler changes, chunked prefill ordering, and load-balancing strategies that keep all pipeline stages saturated.

title: TechCrunch reports SGLang spinout as RadixArk
description: TechCrunch reported that contributors to the open-source SGLang inference engine had formed RadixArk to commercialize services around the project, citing a $400 million valuation as the inference market accelerated. The official launch followed in May.

title: Qwen3 / Qwen3-VL latency optimization on AMD MI300X
description: LMSYS published joint work with the Qwen C-end Infrastructure Engineering Team and the AMD AI Framework Team on Qwen3 and Qwen3-VL latency optimization on AMD MI300X. Reported gains: Qwen3-235B TTFT 1.67x and TPOT 2.12x; Qwen3-VL-235B TTFT 1.62x and TPOT 1.90x — driven by PTPC-FP8 GEMM, attention/MoE kernel fusion, rocJPEG image decode, and ViT data parallelism, all on SGLang.

title: SGLang-Diffusion advanced optimizations for video generation
description: LMSYS shared the next round of SGLang-Diffusion optimizations focused on production-ready video generation: layerwise DiT offload (--dit-layerwise-offload) cutting peak VRAM by up to 30 GB and improving performance up to 58%, Cache-DiT integration up to +165%, plus AMD / RTX 4090 / RTX 5090 support and additional attention/parallelism options.

title: SGLang v0.5.9 released
description: SGLang v0.5.9 shipped LoRA weight-loading overlap, TRT-LLM NSA kernel integration for DeepSeek V3.2, the FlashInfer MoE dispatcher, and FA4 attention support for multimodal encoders, alongside scheduler and stability improvements.

title: SGLang adds day-0 support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super
description: LMSYS and the NVIDIA Nemotron team announced SGLang day-0 support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super, including bf16/fp8/nvfp4 paths and a cookbook for high-efficiency multi-agent system deployments built on the new model family.

title: LMSYS blog: Elastic EP for partial failure tolerance
description: LMSYS Org published a deep dive on Elastic NIXL-EP integration in SGLang, explaining how DeepSeek-style MoE deployments survive single-GPU failures by redistributing expert weights and continuing to serve without a full restart. The blog accompanied SGLang PRs #19248, #17374, and #12068.

title: Highlights of SGLang at NVIDIA GTC 2026
description: LMSYS recapped SGLang's presence at NVIDIA GTC 2026 — joint sessions with NVIDIA on Blackwell deployments (GB200 / GB300 NVL72), DeepSeek-V3.2 acceleration, model-optimizer integration, and the SGLang ecosystem roadmap.

title: SGLang v0.5.10 released
description: SGLang v0.5.10 promoted Piecewise CUDA Graph as the default execution mode, integrated Elastic EP for partial failure tolerance on DeepSeek MoE deployments, added a GPU staging buffer for PD disaggregation (~5x TPS on large concurrency), HiSparse sparse attention, FlashInfer MXFP8 kernels, the Transformers 5.3.0 upgrade, FA4 official library support, native MLX backend for Apple Silicon, and LoRA support for MoE layers.

title: SGLang v0.5.10.post1 patch
description: Patch release that bumped flashinfer from v0.6.7.post2 to v0.6.7.post3 to resolve an issue in its JIT cubin downloader.

title: HiSparse: hierarchical-memory sparse attention
description: LMSYS published HiSparse, a sparse-attention backend that uses hierarchical memory to accelerate long-context inference in SGLang. The post described the algorithm, kernel design, and end-to-end serving wins over dense attention on long-context Llama and DeepSeek workloads.

title: RadixArk launches with $100M seed at $400M valuation
description: RadixArk officially launched with a $100M seed round led by Accel and co-led by Spark Capital at a $400M post-money valuation. Co-founders Ying Sheng (CEO, ex-xAI) and Banghua Zhu (CTO, ex-NVIDIA) said the company will keep growing SGLang and Miles as open-source projects while building managed inference and training infrastructure. Investors include NVentures, AMD, MediaTek, Databricks, John Schulman, Lip-Bu Tan, and Igor Babuschkin.

title: SGLang v0.5.11 released
description: SGLang v0.5.11 made CUDA 13 + PyTorch 2.11 the default build, enabled Speculative Decoding V2 with overlap scheduling by default, shipped a Decode Radix Cache for prefix caching under PD disaggregation, added DFLASH speculative decoding kernels and FA3 alongside FA4, plus day-0 model support for Gemma 4, GLM-5.1, Qwen3.6, MiMo-V2.5/V2.5-Pro, Ling-2.6-Flash, Mistral Medium 3.5, and Kimi-K2.6, and LoRA support for DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi-K2.
